question: What is the main job of the urethra?

options.A: Filtering metabolic waste products from circulating blood plasma
options.B: Producing liquid components that make up seminal fluid
options.C: Conveying urine from the bladder to the body exterior
options.D: Storing urine until voluntary micturition can occur safely

explanation: The urethra acts as the tube that carries urine out of the bladder during urination. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T4#GNS121_U2_T4_h1)

question: In females, which body system uses the urethra exclusively?
explanation: Females have separate openings for reproduction and urination, so the female urethra only serves the urinary system. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T4#GNS121_U2_T4_h1)

question: What is the approximate length of an adult female urethra?
explanation: The female urethra is short, measuring about four centimeters from the bladder to the outside opening. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T4#GNS121_U2_T4_h2)

question: Why does a shorter urethra make it easier for females to get urinary tract infections?

options.A: Urine remains stagnant inside the short conduit longer
options.B: Bacteria travel a shorter distance to reach the bladder
options.C: Hormonal shifts constantly dilate the external opening
options.D: The bladder wall produces less protective mucus in women

explanation: Because the urethra is short, bacteria do not have to travel far to enter the bladder and cause an infection. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T4#GNS121_U2_T4_h2)

question: Which part of the male urethra is surrounded by the prostate gland?
explanation: The prostatic urethra runs directly through the middle of the prostate gland. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T4#GNS121_U2_T4_h3)

question: Which male urethral part is the shortest and least stretchy?
explanation: The membranous segment passes through rigid pelvic floor tissues, making it short and less flexible. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T4#GNS121_U2_T4_h3)

question: What structure lies right behind the female urethra?
explanation: The back wall of the female urethra sits right against the front wall of the vagina. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T4#GNS121_U2_T4_h4)

question: Where is the external opening of the female urethra located?

options.A: Directly on the posterior wall of the bladder
options.B: In the vestibule anterior to the vagina
options.C: Between the labia minora posterior to the anus
options.D: Deep within the anterior vaginal vault

explanation: The external opening of the urethra is found in the vulvar vestibule, right in front of the vaginal opening. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T4#GNS121_U2_T4_h4)

question: What type of tissue lines the part of the urethra closest to the bladder?
explanation: Transitional epithelium lines the upper urethra, matching the lining of the urinary bladder. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T4#GNS121_U2_T4_h5)

question: What kind of cell lining is found near the outer opening of the urethra?
explanation: Stratified squamous epithelium helps protect the outer end of the urethra from friction and irritation. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T4#GNS121_U2_T4_h5)

question: What type of muscle forms the internal urethral sphincter?
explanation: The internal sphincter is made of smooth muscle, which works automatically without conscious control. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T4#GNS121_U2_T4_h6)

question: Which nerve gives you voluntary control over the external urethral sphincter?
explanation: The pudendal nerve supplies the external urethral sphincter, allowing you to consciously control when you urinate. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T4#GNS121_U2_T4_h6)

question: Which major pelvic blood vessel supplies blood to the urethra?
explanation: Branches from the internal iliac artery supply blood to the pelvic organs, including the urethra. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T4#GNS121_U2_T4_h7)

question: Where does the main lymphatic drainage of the urethra go?
explanation: Lymph fluid from the urethra drains mainly into the iliac lymph nodes located in the pelvis. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T4#GNS121_U2_T4_h7)

question: What are the two functions of the male urethra?
explanation: The male urethra is part of both the urinary and reproductive systems, carrying either urine or semen at different times. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T4#GNS121_U2_T4_h8)

question: Why do glands release mucus into the male urethra before ejaculation?

options.A: To cool down the reproductive organs
options.B: To speed up sperm production rates
options.D: To prevent bladder spasms during rest

explanation: Alkaline mucus protects sperm from any leftover acid in the urethra from previous urination. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T4#GNS121_U2_T4_h8)
